Over the past three days, though, his daughter had noticed him becoming increasingly drowsy and forgetful, uncharacteristically slow to answer even simple questions, and this morning he'd seemed genuinely confused about where he was.
background: He takes a blood thinner for an irregular heartbeat, and is otherwise generally well and independent for his age. No other falls recently, no history of memory problems before this week.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Bernard was drowsy but rousable, able to say his own name but not the date or where he was. His temperature was normal, blood pressure 148 over 86, heart rate regular.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: Mild weakness was noted on his left side compared with the right, his pupils were equal and reactive, there was no obvious facial droop, and his reflexes were slightly brisker on the left than the right.

exam.title: Skin/Head
exam.body: A small, fading bruise was visible above his right ear from the fall a week earlier, with no other injuries found anywhere else.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to check for infection and his clotting levels given his blood thinner:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: White cell count and CRP: normal, arguing against an infective cause
Clotting level (INR): above his usual target range, meaning his blood was thinner than intended

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An urgent CT scan of his head was performed:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A crescent-shaped collection of blood along the surface of the right side of the brain
Mild pressure effect on the surrounding brain tissue

treatment: His blood thinner was urgently reversed with medication to correct his clotting, and the neurosurgical team carried out an urgent procedure. Over the following two days, he became noticeably more alert, recognizing his daughter clearly and answering questions correctly again.
discharge: He was discharged after a week of monitoring and physiotherapy, with a careful discussion about the risks and benefits of restarting his blood thinner, and advice for his family on fall-proofing his home to help prevent this happening again.
dd1: Drug overdose or Adverse drug reaction

title: The Long Drive Home
personal: Carol Jennings, 52, Female, 165 cm, 80 kg, school administrator. Admitted to the ambulatory care unit.
incident: Over the past four days, Carol had noticed her left calf becoming increasingly swollen and achy, worse when she'd been standing for a while, with the skin over it feeling warm and slightly tight. She'd blamed it at first on a long car journey the week before and tried elevating her leg at night, but the swelling hadn't improved and, if anything, had gotten a little worse.
background: She'd taken an eight-hour car trip for a family visit recently, has a sedentary desk job, and is on hormone replacement therapy for menopause symptoms. No personal or family history of blood clots, no recent surgery or injury to the leg.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Carol was otherwise well, afebrile, with normal vital signs throughout.

exam.title: Limb examination
exam.body: Her left calf was visibly swollen compared with the right, with a measurable difference in circumference, warm to the touch, and tender along the path of the deep veins behind the knee and down the calf. There was no spreading redness typical of a skin infection, and no fluctuant swelling behind the knee to suggest a ruptured cyst.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to check a clot marker:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: D-dimer: elevated
White cell count and CRP: normal, arguing against an infective cause

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An ultrasound of the leg veins was arranged:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A non-compressible segment identified within the deep vein of the left calf, confirming a clot
Superficial veins and the right leg: entirely normal

treatment: Carol was started on medication and advised to stay as mobile as comfortably possible. Over the following days, the swelling and tenderness in her calf gradually began to settle.
discharge: She went home on ongoing blood thinners for several months, with a discussion about stopping her hormone replacement therapy given the added risk it carries alongside a clot, and advice on moving regularly during any future long journeys.

title: Not Just a Bladder Infection
personal: Bianca Ford, 29, Female, 163 cm, 60 kg, retail manager. Admitted to the acute medical unit.
incident: For the past two days she'd had a burning sensation when urinating and had been going more often than usual — symptoms she recognized from a bladder infection she'd had once before, which she'd tried to manage with cranberry juice and over-the-counter remedies. Today, though, things had taken a turn: a fever set in, along with a deep, aching pain in her right lower back, and she'd been sick twice, unable to keep anything down.
background: One previous simple bladder infection a couple of years ago, treated successfully with antibiotics at the time. No known kidney problems, not pregnant, sexually active with one partner, no known drug allergies.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Bianca looked flushed and unwell, her temperature reading 39.0°C, heart rate 110, blood pressure 108 over 68.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: There was mild generalized tenderness across her abdomen, but the most striking finding came when the doctor gently tapped over her lower right back, just below the ribs — a sharp wince confirmed clear tenderness over that kidney specifically.

exam.title: Abdominal, further
exam.body: The front of her abdomen was otherwise soft, with no rebound or rigidity, and no tenderness over the area where the appendix sits.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: A urine sample and blood tests were sent together:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Urinalysis: significant white cells, blood, and nitrites, all pointing to infection
Urine culture: sent, result pending
White cell count and CRP: both raised
Kidney function: normal

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An ultrasound of her kidneys was arranged:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Right kidney: mildly swollen appearance consistent with infection
No stone identified
No blockage seen

treatment: Bianca was started on intravenous antibiotics and fluids to help with the dehydration from being sick, with her temperature and pain checked regularly. Over the following two days her fever settled, the back pain eased considerably, and she was able to keep food down again.
discharge: She was discharged home to complete a full course of oral antibiotics, with advice on staying well hydrated and returning promptly if the back pain or fever came back, along with a routine follow-up urine test arranged after finishing the course.

title: A Band Across His Forehead
personal: Gerald Simmons, 68, Male, 175 cm, 82 kg, retired accountant. Admitted to the ophthalmology ward.
incident: Four days ago he'd noticed a strange tingling, burning sensation on the right side of his forehead, which he'd put down to a tension headache brought on by stress. Two days later, a cluster of small, fluid-filled blisters appeared across the same area, spreading down toward his right eyelid and the tip of his nose. Today his right eye had turned red and watery and become increasingly sensitive to light, making it hard for him to keep it open at all.
background: No significant past medical history apart from well-controlled high blood pressure. No known immune problems, had chickenpox as a child like most people his age, no recent illness he could point to, though he'd been feeling generally run down over the past couple of weeks.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Gerald was otherwise well and afebrile, mildly uncomfortable from the pain on his forehead.

exam.title: Skin
exam.body: A cluster of vesicles in various stages — some fresh and fluid-filled, others crusted over — was distributed in a clear band across the right forehead and upper eyelid, stopping abruptly at the midline of his face, a distribution doctors immediately recognize as following a single nerve pathway. A few small vesicles were also noted on the tip of his nose, a detail the doctor paid close attention to, since it can signal the eye itself is at risk.

exam.title: Eye examination
exam.body: His right eye was red and watering, with mild sensitivity to light, though his vision remained largely unaffected, and there was no visible cloudiness of the eye itself yet.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Routine bloods were sent, along with a swab from one of the fresh blisters:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: White cell count and CRP: normal, arguing against a bacterial infection like cellulitis
Swab from a vesicle: confirmed the virus responsible for chickenpox and shingles

investigations.title: Eye Examination
investigations.body: An eye examination using a special dye and blue light was performed by the ophthalmology team:

reports.title: Eye Examination Report
lines: No ulceration of the clear front surface of the eye identified at this stage
Mild inflammation of the eye surface noted
Pressure within the eye: normal

treatment: Gerald was started promptly on an antiviral medication in tablet form, along with eye drops to protect and soothe the surface of his eye, and the ophthalmology team monitored him closely over the following days to make sure the deeper structures of the eye remained unaffected. The blisters gradually dried and crusted over, and the redness in his eye slowly began to settle.
discharge: He was discharged on a full course of antiviral tablets with close ophthalmology follow-up arranged over the following weeks, given the small risk of this condition affecting the eye more seriously later on, and advice on avoiding contact with anyone who'd never had chickenpox until the blisters had fully crusted over.

title: Couldn't Take a Deep Breath
personal: Yolanda Reyes, 45, Female, 160 cm, 66 kg, works in accounts, on regular dialysis for kidney failure. Admitted to the cardiology ward.
incident: Over the past week she'd felt increasingly breathless, especially when lying flat, and today felt so short of breath and lightheaded even at rest that her family brought her straight in. She mentioned a vague, dull ache in her chest that had come and gone for several days, and said it felt like she couldn't take a satisfying deep breath no matter how hard she tried.
background: She's on dialysis three times a week for kidney failure, though she admitted to occasionally missing sessions because of work. No known heart disease previously, no recent chest infections or trauma.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Yolanda looked unwell and anxious, breathless even at rest, with a blood pressure of 88 over 60 that dropped further with each breath in. Her heart rate was 118, and the veins in her neck stood out visibly.

exam.title: Cardiovascular
exam.body: Her heart sounds were notably muffled and difficult to hear clearly. The doctor specifically checked her blood pressure through a full breathing cycle and found it dropped significantly more than normal during inspiration — a finding that carries real diagnostic weight in exactly this kind of situation.

exam.title: Respiratory
exam.body: Her lungs were clear on listening, without the crackles that might point toward fluid backing up from ordinary heart failure.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to check her kidney function and heart markers:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Kidney function: significantly impaired, consistent with her known kidney failure
Hemoglobin: mildly low but not severely so
Heart-strain marker: mildly raised

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An urgent echocardiogram was performed:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A large collection of fluid surrounding the heart
The right side of the heart shown partially collapsing with each heartbeat, a sign of the fluid squeezing the heart from outside and preventing it from filling properly

treatment: An urgent needle procedure was carried out with the help of ultrasound, bringing swift relief to her breathing and blood pressure. She was also referred urgently for a review of her dialysis schedule, since how consistently dialysis is carried out can play a part in problems like this.
discharge: She recovered well over the following days, discharged with a much stricter dialysis schedule agreed with her kidney team and closer cardiology follow-up to keep an eye on any fluid building up around her heart again in the future.

title: The Junction Collision
personal: Marcus Webb, 22, Male, 179 cm, 74 kg, university student. Admitted to the trauma ward following a car accident.
incident: He'd been the front-seat passenger in a car that collided with another vehicle at a junction earlier that evening, his side of the car taking the brunt of the impact against the door. He'd been conscious throughout, complaining mainly of pain on his left side under the ribs, and had begun feeling increasingly dizzy and unwell in the back of the ambulance on the way in.
background: No significant past medical history. He was wearing his seatbelt at the time of the crash, had no loss of consciousness, and paramedics noted no other obvious injuries at the scene.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Marcus was pale and increasingly anxious, his blood pressure dropping to 92 over 58 and his heart rate climbing to 120, though he was still talking normally.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: There was marked tenderness over the left upper abdomen under the ribs, with mild guarding, and he reported a subtle ache in his left shoulder tip when the doctor pressed there — a sign, again, of irritation reaching up under the diaphragm from bleeding lower down.

exam.title: Chest
exam.body: There was no obvious bruising or deformity over his ribs, his chest expanded equally on both sides, and breath sounds were present and equal throughout.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent urgently for a full count and crossmatch given the concern for internal bleeding:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Hemoglobin: falling on repeat testing
Group & crossmatch: urgent request sent
Kidney function: normal, arguing somewhat against a significant kidney injury

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: A CT scan of his chest, abdomen, and pelvis with contrast was arranged once he was stable enough to go:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Spleen: a laceration identified, with a moderate amount of blood pooling around it in the abdomen
Kidneys: both intact and uninjured
No other significant internal injuries identified

treatment: Given how his blood pressure and heart rate were trending, the team elected to monitor him extremely closely in a high-dependency setting with blood held ready, rather than rush straight to surgery, since injuries like this can often settle on their own if the bleeding stops. His numbers stabilized over the following hours without needing surgery or transfusion.
discharge: After several days of monitoring, with repeat scans confirming things were settling as hoped, Marcus was discharged with strict instructions to avoid any contact sports or heavy lifting for several weeks while the injury fully healed, and clear guidance on symptoms that should bring him straight back in.

title: Rings Around the Lamp
personal: Susan Whitcombe, 63, Female, 162 cm, 70 kg, retired bank clerk. Admitted to the ophthalmology ward via the emergency department.
incident: While watching television in a dimly lit room that evening, Susan developed a sudden, severe pain in her right eye that quickly spread into a pounding headache on that side, along with blurred vision and the sight of colored rings around the lamp across the room. Within the hour she felt increasingly nauseated and was sick twice, which briefly made her wonder if she was coming down with a stomach bug rather than anything to do with her eye.
background: No previous eye problems apart from needing reading glasses for several years, no known family history of eye disease that she was aware of, and no recent head injury. She mentioned she'd been particularly farsighted her whole life, something a family member later recalled a doctor once linking to a slightly increased risk of this kind of eye problem.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Susan was clearly distressed by the pain, otherwise well, afebrile, with a normal blood pressure.

exam.title: Eye examination
exam.body: The right eye appeared visibly red, with a cloudy-looking cornea and a pupil that was mid-sized and fixed, not reacting normally to light the way the left pupil did. Gently feeling the eye through closed lids, it felt notably firmer than the other side.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: There was no weakness, no facial droop, and no other neurological findings, making a stroke or significant neurological cause far less likely.

investigations.title: Eye Pressure
investigations.body: The pressure inside her eye was measured directly by the ophthalmology team:

reports.title: Eye Pressure Report
lines: Right eye: markedly elevated pressure, well above the normal range
Left eye: normal pressure

investigations.title: Eye Examination
investigations.body: A closer examination of the drainage angle inside the eye was performed using a special lens:

reports.title: Eye Examination Report
lines: Drainage angle of the right eye: closed, preventing fluid from draining properly and explaining the high pressure

treatment: Susan was given medication directly into the eye and through a vein to treat the problem urgently, along with pain relief and anti-sickness medication. Once things had settled, a small laser procedure was performed to prevent the problem coming back. Her pain and blurred vision began easing within hours.
discharge: She was discharged with eye drops to continue in both eyes, since the same problem can develop in the other eye later on, and the same preventive laser procedure was arranged for her left eye shortly afterward to head off any future episode there too.

title: Colder Than He Realized
personal: Malik Johnson, 24, Male, 178 cm, 70 kg, warehouse worker, known sickle cell disease. Admitted to the acute medical unit.
incident: He woke in the middle of the night with a severe, deep aching pain in both thighs and his lower back — pain he recognized immediately from past episodes, though this one felt worse than usual. Alongside it, a tight, aching pain had settled across his chest, bad enough that taking a full breath hurt. He'd been at a friend's outdoor barbecue the evening before in unusually cold weather without a jacket, something he knows can sometimes set these episodes off.
background: Diagnosed with sickle cell disease since childhood, Malik has had several similar pain episodes over the years, usually managed with strong pain relief and fluids at home. His last hospital admission for this was about eight months ago. No recent infections that he's aware of, and he takes a folic acid supplement regularly.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Malik was visibly in significant pain, grimacing with every movement. His temperature read 37.9°C, heart rate 112, blood pressure 128 over 78, respiratory rate 22, with mild pallor visible in his conjunctivae in keeping with his chronic anemia.

exam.title: Musculoskeletal
exam.body: There was tenderness over both thighs and his lower back to palpation, with no swelling, warmth, or redness over any specific joint that might point toward a localized bone infection instead.

exam.title: Respiratory
exam.body: He reported mild tenderness over his chest wall on deep breathing, though his chest sounded clear to listen to, with his oxygen saturation slightly below his usual baseline at 94%.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to check his baseline counts and look for signs of a complication:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Hemoglobin: at his usual low baseline
Reticulocyte count: elevated, in keeping with his chronic condition
White cell count: mildly raised
CRP: mildly raised

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: Given the chest symptoms, a chest X-ray was arranged to check closely for the more dangerous complication being watched for:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Lungs: clear, no new infiltrate or consolidation

treatment: Malik was started on strong pain relief through a drip, warmed blankets, and generous fluids to help the crisis pass, with his oxygen levels and breathing checked frequently given the concern about his chest. Over the following two days, the pain in his legs and back gradually eased, and his oxygen levels crept back up to his usual baseline.
discharge: He was discharged once his pain was controlled on tablets alone, with his usual sickle cell team following up to review his prevention plan and talk through what might have triggered this particular episode.

title: Bruises Without a Story
personal: Zara Ahmed, 6, Female, 116 cm, 21 kg, primary school student. Admitted to the pediatric oncology ward.
incident: For the past three weeks, Zara's parents had noticed her becoming increasingly tired, less interested in playing with her friends, and pale in a way that worried her mother more than the usual sniffles of a school-age child. Over the past week, unexplained bruises had appeared on her legs and arms without any memory of bumping into anything, and yesterday her gums bled a little while brushing her teeth. This morning she woke with a fever, complaining that her legs ached.
background: Previously a healthy, active child with no significant medical history, up to date on immunizations, no recent unusual infections — though she'd had a mild cold about a month ago that seemed to resolve normally at the time.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Zara was pale, quiet, and withdrawn compared with how her mother described her usual energy. Her temperature read 38.1°C, heart rate 110, with mild pallor visible in her lips and inner eyelids.

exam.title: Skin
exam.body: Multiple bruises of different ages were scattered across both shins and forearms, along with a few tiny pinpoint red spots on her lower legs, without any clear history of trauma to explain them.

exam.title: Abdominal/Lymphatic
exam.body: Gentle palpation of her abdomen revealed a mildly enlarged spleen, and small, painless swollen lymph nodes were felt in her neck and under her arms.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: A full blood count and blood film were sent urgently:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: White cell count: markedly abnormal, with a large number of immature cells seen on the blood film
Hemoglobin: low
Platelets: markedly low
All three blood cell lines affected together, rather than just one

investigations.title: Bone marrow sampling
investigations.body: Given the blood film findings, a bone marrow sample was taken:

reports.title: Bone Marrow Report
lines: Marrow replaced by a large population of immature, abnormal cells, confirming the source of her low blood counts

treatment: Zara was started on a carefully planned course of treatment under a specialist pediatric team, alongside supportive treatments including blood and platelet transfusions and medication to protect against infection while her own immune system was suppressed by the treatment. Over the following weeks, her energy slowly began to return between treatment cycles, and the bruising on her skin gradually faded.
discharge: She continued her chemotherapy as planned through repeated outpatient visits and shorter hospital stays, with her family supported by the pediatric oncology team throughout what would be a long road of treatment ahead, and an early, encouraging response noted on her first check of the abnormal cells.

title: A Grey Filter Over One Eye
personal: Hannah Price, 27, Female, 166 cm, 62 kg, graphic designer. Admitted for neurology assessment.
incident: Over the past three days, Hannah had noticed the vision in her left eye becoming increasingly blurry and dim, as though someone had put a grey filter over that eye alone. Moving that eye around brought a dull ache behind it that she hadn't experienced before. She'd initially thought she just needed new glasses, but when the blurriness didn't improve and colors — especially reds — started looking washed out through that eye, she decided to get it checked.
background: No significant past medical history, though on further questioning she recalled a strange episode about a year ago of tingling and slight weakness in her right hand that lasted a couple of weeks and resolved completely on its own — something she'd never mentioned to a doctor at the time, assuming it was nothing. No family history of neurological disease that she was aware of.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Hannah was otherwise well, afebrile, with normal vital signs.

exam.title: Eye examination
exam.body: Visual acuity in her left eye was reduced compared with the right, colors appeared notably washed out and less vivid through the left eye when tested formally, and pain was reproduced when she moved that eye in any direction. Shining a light between her two eyes revealed the left pupil didn't constrict quite as briskly as the right — a specific and telling sign.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: The rest of her neurological examination was largely normal, though very subtle differences in reflexes were noted between her left and right sides when tested carefully.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An MRI scan of her brain and the nerves behind her eyes was arranged:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Inflammation identified along the optic nerve of the left eye
Several additional small areas of abnormality scattered elsewhere within the brain's white matter, in a pattern typical of a particular demyelinating condition

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: A lumbar puncture was performed to sample the fluid around her brain and spinal cord:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Specific proteins (oligoclonal bands) detected in the spinal fluid but not in a matched blood sample, a pattern supporting inflammation localized within the nervous system itself

treatment: Hannah was given a short course of high-dose steroids through a vein to help calm the inflammation affecting her optic nerve and speed her visual recovery, alongside a thorough explanation from the neurology team of what the scan and other results meant and what the road ahead might look like. Her vision began to improve gradually over the following two weeks.
discharge: She was discharged with vision much improved, though not entirely back to normal yet, and referred to a specialist team to discuss long-term treatment options aimed at reducing the frequency of future episodes like this one.

title: Too Unwell for Work
personal: Nadia Osei, 34, Female, 164 cm, 71 kg, hairdresser. Admitted to the gynecology ward.
incident: For about a week she'd had a nagging, worsening pain low in her pelvis on both sides, along with an unpleasant vaginal discharge she'd been putting off dealing with, hoping it would clear up on its own. Over the past two days the pain had become far more severe and constant, accompanied by fevers and chills, and today she felt too unwell to go to work, doubled over and unable to find a comfortable position.
background: A history of pelvic inflammatory disease diagnosed and treated about two years ago, not entirely consistent with using barrier contraception since then, currently between regular partners, no known pregnancy, last period two weeks ago and normal.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Nadia looked unwell and febrile at 38.7°C, heart rate 116, blood pressure 106 over 68.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: There was marked tenderness across her lower abdomen on both sides, worse on the right, with voluntary guarding but no rigid, board-like abdomen.

exam.title: Pelvic, chaperoned
exam.body: Significant pain occurred on moving the cervix from side to side, and a tender, poorly defined swelling was felt on the right side, seeming larger and firmer than would be expected from the ovary alone. A foul-smelling discharge was noted.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood and a pregnancy test were sent, along with swabs from the discharge:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Urine β-hCG: negative
White cell count and CRP: both markedly elevated
Vaginal swabs: sent for culture, result pending

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An ultrasound of her pelvis was arranged:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A complex, fluid-filled mass involving the right ovary and adjacent fallopian tube, consistent with a walled-off collection of pus
Left side: mildly inflamed appearance, no distinct collection

treatment: Nadia was started on a combination of intravenous antibiotics targeting the likely range of bacteria responsible, with close monitoring of her fever and pain. When her response to antibiotics alone proved slower than hoped after 48 hours, a drain was placed through the skin under imaging guidance, after which her fever and pain both improved rapidly.
discharge: She completed a longer course of oral antibiotics after leaving hospital, with a follow-up scan arranged to confirm the collection had fully resolved, and a frank discussion with the gynecology team about future fertility and the importance of prompt treatment for any similar symptoms going forward.

title: Eyes That Wouldn't Sit Still
personal: Colin Yates, 47, Male, 174 cm, 68 kg, unemployed, long history of heavy alcohol use. Admitted to the acute medical unit.
incident: His sister, who checks on him periodically, found him at home unsteady on his feet, bumping into furniture, and speaking in a way that didn't quite make sense — repeating himself and seeming unusually confused about the day and time. She also noticed his eyes seemed to be flickering back and forth in a way she'd never seen before, and, judging by the state of his kitchen, he'd barely eaten anything in days.
background: A long history of heavy daily alcohol use for over fifteen years, poor and irregular eating habits, no known other medical conditions though he hasn't seen a doctor in years, and no recent falls or head injury that his sister was aware of.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Colin had a thin, unkempt appearance and was mildly unsteady even sitting on the edge of the bed. His temperature was normal, with blood pressure and heart rate both mildly elevated.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: An unsteady, wide-based gait was noted when he attempted to walk, along with abnormal back-and-forth eye movements when asked to follow a finger, and confusion when asked simple questions about the date, his location, and recent events.

exam.title: Abdominal/Skin
exam.body: There was no yellowing of his skin or eyes, and his abdomen was soft without obvious swelling that might suggest fluid buildup from liver disease.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to check his liver function and other markers:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Liver function tests: mildly deranged but not severely so, arguing somewhat against a liver-driven cause
Blood alcohol level: elevated but not extremely high
Blood glucose: normal
Ammonia level: normal, further arguing against a liver-related cause

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: A CT scan of his head was performed to rule out a structural cause:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: No bleeding, no mass, no evidence of a stroke

treatment: Colin was started immediately on a high-dose treatment through a vein. Over the following two days, his eye movements returned to normal and his balance improved noticeably, though his confusion took a little longer to clear.
discharge: He was discharged on ongoing oral vitamin supplementation, with support offered for alcohol reduction services and a referral to a dietitian, along with a clear explanation to him and his sister of the importance of continuing the vitamin replacement and improving his diet going forward.

title: The Crack That Wouldn't Heal
personal: Rebecca Holt, 29, Female, 165 cm, 68 kg, new mother, four weeks postpartum. Admitted to the maternity ward.
incident: Over the past two days her right breast had become increasingly painful, red, and hot to the touch, particularly in one area, and overnight she'd developed a fever with shivering fits that left her exhausted. She mentioned her baby had been struggling to latch properly on that side recently, and she'd noticed a small crack in her nipple that had been slow to heal.
background: First-time mother, breastfeeding exclusively, no previous breast problems, no known allergies, uncomplicated vaginal delivery four weeks ago.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Rebecca looked tired and unwell, with a temperature of 38.9°C, heart rate 108, otherwise stable.

exam.title: Breast examination
exam.body: The right breast was diffusely red, warm, and swollen, with one particular area feeling firmer and more tender than the rest. Gently pressing on that firmer area produced a sense of fluctuation under the skin, suggesting fluid had collected there rather than the redness being from inflammation alone.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to check for signs of significant infection:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: White cell count: raised
CRP: elevated

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An ultrasound of the affected breast was arranged to look directly at the firm area:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A defined fluid collection within the right breast, consistent with a localized pocket of pus, separate from the surrounding inflamed but otherwise normal breast tissue

treatment: Rebecca was started on antibiotics, and a fine-needle procedure was carried out under ultrasound guidance, avoiding the need for a more invasive operation. She was supported by a lactation consultant to keep breastfeeding or expressing from both sides where possible, since continuing to remove milk actually helps the area heal. Her fever settled within a day of the drainage, and the redness and swelling gradually began to reduce.
discharge: She completed a course of oral antibiotics at home, with a follow-up ultrasound arranged to confirm the collection hadn't reaccumulated, and ongoing support from the lactation team to help with positioning and latch to prevent this happening again.

title: Stabbed From Inside
personal: Trevor Yang, 61, Male, 170 cm, 74 kg, retired postal worker. Admitted to the general surgical ward via the emergency department.
incident: He'd been sitting at home reading when a sudden, severe pain tore through his upper abdomen, described as feeling like being stabbed, spreading rapidly across his entire belly within the hour. Any movement at all made it dramatically worse, and he found himself lying as still as possible, breathing in shallow little breaths because even that hurt.
background: A longstanding history of indigestion and occasional upper abdominal discomfort, self-treated with over-the-counter antacids, regular use of over-the-counter anti-inflammatory painkillers for chronic knee pain, no previous surgeries, no formally diagnosed ulcers before today, moderate alcohol use.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Trevor lay completely still, pale and sweating, breathing shallowly. His blood pressure read 100 over 64, heart rate 118, temperature 37.8°C.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: His abdomen was rigid throughout, board-like to touch, with pain on the gentlest pressure everywhere, and marked rebound tenderness across the whole abdomen rather than one specific area — findings consistent with widespread irritation of the lining of the abdominal cavity.

exam.title: Cardiovascular
exam.body: Heart sounds were normal, no murmurs, equal pulses in both arms.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An erect chest X-ray was taken first, a quick and simple test for exactly this kind of concern:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A thin crescent of free air visible beneath the diaphragm, indicating a hole somewhere in the gut allowing air to escape into the abdominal cavity

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent alongside the imaging:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: White cell count: markedly raised
Amylase/lipase: mildly raised, but not to the degree typically seen with pancreatitis
Lactate: mildly elevated

treatment: Trevor was taken to theatre without delay, where the surgical team repaired what they found and washed out the abdominal cavity thoroughly. He was kept on strong antibiotics and closely monitored in the days that followed, gradually able to start sipping fluids again as his bowel function returned.
discharge: He was discharged after a week in hospital, with the anti-inflammatory painkillers he'd been taking for his knee stopped for good and a different approach agreed for his pain relief, along with a course of treatment to eradicate the stomach bacterium found to be a common driver of ulcers like his.

title: Tall, Thin, and Suddenly Breathless
personal: Owen Fletcher, 20, Male, 188 cm, 68 kg, university student. Brought into the resuscitation area.
incident: While playing five-a-side football, Owen suddenly felt a sharp, tearing pain on the right side of his chest, unrelated to any collision or fall, and within minutes found himself increasingly breathless, gasping for air in a way that alarmed his teammates. By the time he was brought to hospital he could barely speak in full sentences, and one of the paramedics noted his neck veins looked unusually prominent.
background: No history of chest trauma, no known lung disease, though his mother mentioned he'd always been unusually tall and thin for his age. Non-smoker, no family history of anything similar that anyone could recall.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Owen was visibly distressed, gasping for breath, unable to complete full sentences. His blood pressure had dropped to 84 over 52, heart rate 132, with the veins in his neck visibly bulging.

exam.title: Respiratory
exam.body: No breath sounds at all could be heard over the right side of his chest, compared with normal breath sounds on the left, and tapping over the right side produced an unusually hollow, drum-like sound. His windpipe, normally sitting centrally at the base of his neck, was found pushed noticeably toward the left side.

exam.title: Cardiovascular
exam.body: Heart sounds were faint but present, consistent with the chest findings rather than a primary heart problem, without the muffling pattern typical of fluid around the heart itself.

investigations.title: Emergency Procedure
investigations.body: Given how unstable he was, the emergency team did not wait for imaging and treated the diagnosis immediately based on the examination findings alone — a decision confirmed correct once the emergency treatment was performed:

reports.title: Emergency Procedure Report
lines: Immediate release of trapped air from the right side of the chest, with a large volume of air escaping under pressure, consistent with the suspected diagnosis

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: A chest X-ray was taken shortly after the emergency treatment to confirm and guide further management:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Right lung: partially re-expanded following the emergency treatment
A chest drain visible in good position
No other injury identified

treatment: A needle was inserted urgently into the right side of Owen's chest bringing immediate relief to his breathing and blood pressure, followed shortly after by a proper chest tube placed over the following days. He improved dramatically within minutes of the first needle.
discharge: Once the chest tube was removed and a follow-up X-ray confirmed his lung had fully re-expanded, Owen was discharged with advice to avoid flying or scuba diving for a period of time, information about the small chance of this happening again given his build, and clear guidance on symptoms that should prompt him to seek help urgently.

title: Pushed Forward
personal: Leo Marchetti, 5, Male, 110 cm, 19 kg, kindergartener. Admitted to the pediatric ward.
incident: Leo had been treated for an ear infection about ten days ago with a course of antibiotics from his family doctor, and had seemed to improve initially. Over the past three days, though, his ear pain had returned worse than before, along with a fever, and yesterday his mother noticed the area behind his ear had become red, swollen, and tender, with his ear itself appearing to stick out further than usual on that side.
background: This was his third ear infection this year, with previous episodes resolving fully with antibiotics before, without any complications like this. No known allergies, up to date on immunizations, generally a healthy and active child.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Leo was miserable and clingy to his mother, with a temperature of 39.0°C, heart rate 118, otherwise alert and interactive.

exam.title: Ear examination
exam.body: The right ear canal and eardrum looked inflamed and bulging, consistent with an ongoing ear infection, while the skin over the bone just behind that ear was red, swollen, warm, and tender to touch, with the ear itself pushed forward and outward compared with the normal position on the other side.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: There was no facial weakness on either side, no neck stiffness, and he was alert and responding appropriately to questions for his age.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to check for signs of a deeper infection:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: White cell count: markedly raised
CRP: markedly elevated

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: A CT scan of his head was arranged to look at the bone behind the ear:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: The bony air cells behind the right ear filled with fluid and showing early erosion of the surrounding bone, consistent with infection having spread beyond the middle ear into the bone itself
No collection of pus outside the bone identified

treatment: Leo was admitted for intravenous antibiotics targeting the infection more aggressively than the oral course he'd had before, with the ENT team monitoring him closely for any sign of the infection spreading further, which would have needed a surgical procedure to address directly. Over the following three days, his fever settled, the swelling behind his ear reduced, and his ear returned to its normal position.
discharge: He completed a longer course of antibiotics at home after leaving hospital, with a follow-up ENT appointment arranged to check his hearing and make sure the infection had fully cleared, along with a discussion about whether grommets might help reduce how often he gets ear infections going forward.

title: Sunburned Without the Sun
personal: Isabelle Carter, 19, Female, 165 cm, 58 kg, university student. Admitted to the intensive care unit.
incident: She woke up two days into her period feeling suddenly and dramatically unwell — a high fever, widespread muscle aches, and a strange sunburn-like rash spreading across her torso and thighs. Over the following hours she became increasingly dizzy and weak, vomiting twice and developing diarrhea, and her roommate found her slumped against the bathroom wall, too weak to stand, and called for help immediately.
background: Previously fit and healthy, using a high-absorbency tampon which she admitted she'd left in place longer than recommended due to a busy exam schedule. No known allergies, no recent illness or surgery, not on any regular medications.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Isabelle was unwell and lethargic, temperature 39.6°C, blood pressure dropping to 78 over 48, heart rate 132, appearing dehydrated and weak.

exam.title: Skin
exam.body: A diffuse, red, sunburn-like rash covered her trunk, arms, and thighs, blanching when pressed, without the small, non-blanching purple spots that would point toward a different, more sinister cause of a rash with fever.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: There was mild generalized tenderness, no rigidity, and no localized findings, consistent with the widespread illness rather than a specific abdominal source.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent urgently, along with removal of the retained tampon and a swab from the area:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: White cell count: markedly raised
Kidney and liver function: both mildly impaired, consistent with the whole body being under significant strain
Blood cultures: sent
Vaginal swab: sent to look for the bacterium and toxin responsible for this specific condition

investigations.title: Laboratory (excluding an alternative cause)
investigations.body: Blood was also sent looking specifically for the bacterium responsible for the other serious possibility being considered:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Blood culture and specific testing for the meningococcal bacterium: negative

treatment: Isabelle was started immediately on aggressive intravenous fluids to support her blood pressure, along with antibiotics and close monitoring in intensive care given how unwell she'd become. Her blood pressure gradually stabilized over the following day, and the rash and fever began to settle over the following two to three days as the underlying cause was brought under control.
discharge: She was discharged after several days once fully stable, with clear education about tampon use, changing frequency, and early warning signs to watch for, along with advice that she may need to avoid tampons altogether going forward given her history.

title: Fevers Like Clockwork
personal: Daniel Osei-Mensah, 35, Male, 180 cm, 82 kg, engineer. Admitted to the infectious diseases ward.
incident: He'd returned five days ago from a three-week work trip to a rural part of West Africa. Yesterday evening he began experiencing sudden shaking chills so severe his teeth chattered, followed an hour later by a burning fever, drenching sweats, and a pounding headache. He'd assumed it was just jet lag catching up with him until the fevers started coming in waves, roughly a day apart, each one leaving him utterly wrung out.
background: He took antimalarial tablets at the start of the trip but admits he stopped taking them partway through, finding them upsetting to his stomach and assuming the risk was low since he was staying mostly indoors for work. No other recent travel, no prior episodes like this, no chronic illnesses, up to date on other travel vaccines.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Daniel was flushed and sweating profusely between chills, his temperature peaking at 40.1°C, heart rate 118, blood pressure 100 over 62, looking exhausted.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: Mild tenderness was felt in the left upper abdomen where the spleen sits, with the doctor able to feel the edge of a mildly enlarged spleen just below the ribs, otherwise his abdomen was soft.

exam.title: Skin
exam.body: No rash was noted anywhere on his body, which the doctor specifically checked for, since its presence or absence helps distinguish between a few of the possibilities being considered.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent urgently, including a specific test to look directly for the parasite responsible:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Blood film: parasites identified within red blood cells, confirming the diagnosis directly
Platelet count: low
Hemoglobin: mildly reduced
Liver function: mildly deranged

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Blood cultures for typhoid-causing bacteria: no growth
Kidney function: normal, reassuring given how severe this particular infection can occasionally become

treatment: Daniel was started immediately on a course of targeted medication chosen to match what his blood film had shown, along with fluids and close monitoring of his blood counts and organ function given the risk of this illness worsening quickly. Over the following two days, the wave-like fevers settled into something milder and eventually stopped altogether, and his energy slowly began to return.
discharge: He completed his full course of antimalarial treatment, with follow-up blood tests arranged to confirm the parasite had fully cleared, and detailed advice for any future travel about completing preventive medication for the whole recommended course, stomach upset and all.

title: Just the Hot Weather
personal: Patricia Nolan, 74, Female, 160 cm, 78 kg, retired seamstress, known type 2 diabetes. Admitted to the intensive care unit.
incident: Her son, calling to check in as he does every few days, found her answering the phone in a confused, slurred manner that alarmed him enough to drive straight over. He found her at home, drowsy and disoriented, complaining she'd been feeling increasingly thirsty and needing to urinate constantly over the past week, though she'd shrugged it off as "just the hot weather." She'd been eating and drinking very little for the past two days after a bout of a mild stomach upset.
background: Type 2 diabetes managed with tablets for the past twelve years, generally reasonable control though her son admits she sometimes forgets doses. Mild kidney impairment was noted at her last check-up. She lives alone and manages independently most of the time.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Patricia was drowsy, difficult to rouse fully, with very dry mucous membranes and reduced skin turgor. Temperature 37.6°C, heart rate 118, blood pressure 92 over 58.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: She was confused, unable to answer simple orientation questions correctly, with no focal weakness on either side and pupils equal and reactive.

exam.title: Respiratory/Cardiovascular
exam.body: Her breathing was normal in depth and rate, without the deep, labored breathing sometimes seen with a different diabetic emergency. Chest clear, heart sounds normal.

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Blood glucose: extremely elevated, well above what's typically seen even in poorly controlled diabetes
Serum osmolality: markedly elevated
Ketones: absent or only trace, notably different from a different, more acidotic diabetic emergency
Blood pH: within normal range
Kidney function: significantly impaired, worse than her baseline
Urinalysis: no signs of infection

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: A CT scan of her head was performed given her confusion, to rule out a separate cause:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: No evidence of a stroke, no bleeding, no mass

treatment: Patricia was started on very careful, gradual intravenous fluid replacement alongside a slow, steady insulin infusion, with her blood sugar, sodium levels, and kidney function checked frequently throughout, since bringing the levels down too quickly in this particular condition can itself cause harm. Over the following two days, as her blood levels normalized gradually, she became progressively more alert, eventually recognizing her son and able to hold a normal conversation again.
discharge: She was discharged home once stable, with a review of her diabetes medications and a plan for closer monitoring, along with a chat with her son about arrangements to check on her more frequently, especially during any future illness.

title: Cold From the Knee Down
personal: Roger Ainsworth, 68, Male, 176 cm, 88 kg, retired plumber, known atrial fibrillation. Admitted to the vascular surgery ward.
incident: About four hours ago, while gardening, his left foot and lower leg suddenly became intensely painful, cold, and started to feel numb, developing a pale, almost waxy look that alarmed his wife the moment she saw it. He described the pain as coming on abruptly, unlike anything gradual, and within an hour he'd noticed he could barely move his toes on that side.
background: Known atrial fibrillation for several years, prescribed a blood thinner that he admits he's been inconsistent with taking. No previous episodes like this, no smoking, mild high blood pressure controlled with medication, no known peripheral vascular disease previously diagnosed.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Roger was anxious, otherwise stable, apart from an irregularly irregular pulse confirming his known heart rhythm problem.

exam.title: Limb examination
exam.body: The left foot and lower leg were notably paler and colder than the right side, with reduced sensation to light touch over the foot, marked weakness moving his toes, and — most tellingly — no pulses at all could be felt anywhere below the level of his knee on that side, compared with normal pulses easily found on the right.

exam.title: Cardiovascular
exam.body: Irregularly irregular rhythm confirming atrial fibrillation, no murmurs, pulses normal and easily felt throughout the rest of his body.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: Given how time-critical this diagnosis is for saving the limb, imaging was arranged immediately alongside the clinical assessment:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A blood clot identified blocking one of the main arteries supplying the lower leg, with reduced blood flow visible to the tissues beyond the blockage

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Clotting screen: sent given his blood thinner history, showing his levels were below where they should have been for adequate protection
Creatine kinase: mildly elevated, suggesting the muscle tissue was beginning to feel the strain of reduced blood flow

treatment: Roger was taken urgently to theatre, where the vascular surgical team used a specialized catheter to restore blood flow to his leg. His pain eased and the color returned to his foot within hours of the procedure, and his blood-thinning medication was restarted and carefully optimized afterward.
discharge: He was discharged with his leg fully recovered and viable, on a stricter and more closely monitored blood-thinning regimen going forward, with a clear conversation about the importance of taking it consistently given what had almost happened to his leg.

title: The Mirror Wouldn't Lie
personal: Michelle Turner, 40, Female, 165 cm, 64 kg, marketing consultant. Admitted for neurology assessment.
incident: She woke yesterday morning to find the right side of her face wouldn't move properly — unable to close her right eye fully, her smile pulling noticeably to one side, and food and drink escaping from the corner of her mouth when she tried to eat breakfast. She'd gone to bed feeling completely normal the night before, apart from a mild ache behind her right ear that she hadn't thought much of.
background: No significant past medical history, no recent illness apart from a mild cold about a week ago, no known diabetes, no rash noticed anywhere, no recent tick bites or outdoor activity in wooded areas that she could recall.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Michelle was otherwise well, afebrile, with normal vital signs, and clearly distressed by how her face looked in the mirror.

exam.title: Neurological — cranial nerves
exam.body: The right side of her face was weak from her forehead down to her mouth — notably including her forehead, which didn't wrinkle when she tried to raise her eyebrows, a detail doctors pay close attention to since a stroke typically spares the forehead while this condition does not. Her right eye couldn't close completely. The rest of her limbs and the left side of her face were entirely normal.

exam.title: Ear/Skin
exam.body: No vesicles or rash were seen in or around her right ear, and no rash elsewhere on her body suggestive of Lyme disease.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: Given how classic the pattern of weakness was, the priority was simply confirming a stroke wasn't the underlying cause:

reports.title: Imaging Report (CT head)
lines: No evidence of a stroke, no bleeding, no mass

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Lyme disease antibody testing: negative
Blood glucose: normal

treatment: Michelle was started on a short course of oral steroids to reduce the swelling around the affected nerve, along with careful advice on protecting her right eye with lubricating drops and a patch at night to prevent it drying out while she couldn't blink fully. Over the following two weeks, she began to notice small improvements, first in being able to close her eye a little, then gradually more movement returning across the rest of her face.
discharge: She was discharged the same day with her steroid course and eye protection plan, along with a follow-up appointment to check her progress, and reassurance that the great majority of people with this condition make a full or near-full recovery over the following weeks to months.

title: The Peanut at the Party
personal: Toby Reid, 2, Male, 90 cm, 13 kg, toddler. Admitted to the pediatric emergency department.
incident: While snacking on peanuts left within reach at a family gathering, Toby suddenly began coughing forcefully, his face turning red then a worrying shade of blue for a few seconds before the coughing brought some relief. Since then, about two hours ago now, he's had an odd, persistent wheeze his mother has never heard from him before, along with occasional bouts of coughing, though he's otherwise been playing and seems in good spirits between episodes.
background: Previously entirely well, no history of asthma or wheezing before today, up to date on immunizations, no known allergies. This was the first time he'd been given whole peanuts rather than a smoother, safer form of nut.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Toby was alert and playful between episodes, with no fever, and an oxygen saturation slightly reduced at 95% on room air.

exam.title: Respiratory
exam.body: A one-sided wheeze was heard clearly over the right side of his chest, distinctly quieter and different from the left, with reduced air entry noted specifically on that right side compared with normal, full air entry on the left — an asymmetry that doesn't fit well with the more generalized wheeze usually heard with the other possibilities being considered.

exam.title: ENT
exam.body: No stridor, no drooling, no signs of an upper airway problem, and his voice sounded entirely normal.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: A chest X-ray was taken, including a special additional view sometimes used specifically when this diagnosis is suspected in young children:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: The right lung appeared to stay unusually inflated and failed to empty normally on the additional view, compared with the left side, a pattern consistent with something obstructing the airway on that side and trapping air behind it

investigations.title: Airway Examination
investigations.body: Given how strongly the examination and imaging pointed toward this diagnosis, the team proceeded to a direct look inside the airway using a small camera under anesthesia:

reports.title: Airway Examination Report
lines: A peanut fragment identified lodged within the airway leading to the right lung, fully explaining the one-sided wheeze and trapped air

treatment: With Toby safely asleep under anesthesia, the team used a small camera to look into his airways and deal with what they found. His breathing was checked closely as he woke up, and the one-sided wheeze that had worried his mother was gone entirely.
discharge: He was observed for a few hours to make sure his breathing stayed settled, then discharged home the same day, with his parents given clear, practical advice about age-appropriate food textures and the importance of supervising young children closely around nuts, grapes, and other similarly risky foods.

title: Three Weeks of Ear Drops
personal: Harold Vance, 71, Male, 172 cm, 80 kg, retired mechanic, known type 2 diabetes. Admitted to the ENT ward.
incident: For the past three weeks he's had worsening pain and discharge from his right ear, initially treated by his family doctor as a simple outer ear infection with ear drops, which helped only a little before the pain crept steadily worse. Over the past few days, the pain has become severe, keeping him up at night, and today he noticed the right side of his face felt slightly different, less mobile, when he tried to smile.
background: Type 2 diabetes for over twenty years, admits his blood sugar control has been poor for a long stretch of that time. No known hearing problems previously, no swimming or water exposure recently that might explain a simple outer ear infection lasting this long.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Harold was otherwise reasonably well, mildly uncomfortable from the ear pain, temperature 37.7°C, with a bedside blood glucose check markedly elevated.

exam.title: Ear examination
exam.body: The ear canal was swollen, red, and markedly tender, with a small amount of discharge and, notably, an area of raw, granulation-type tissue visible at the junction where the ear canal meets the bone of the skull — a finding doctors take very seriously in someone with his particular combination of risk factors.

exam.title: Neurological — cranial nerves
exam.body: Mild weakness was noted on the right side of his face, involving his forehead as well as the lower part of his face, suggesting the facial nerve running close to that area was becoming involved by whatever process was affecting his ear.

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: White cell count: mildly raised
CRP and ESR: both markedly elevated
HbA1c: significantly above target, reflecting poor long-term sugar control
Ear discharge swab: sent for culture

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: A CT scan, followed by a specialized nuclear medicine scan, was arranged to look at the bone at the base of his skull:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Early erosion of the bone at the base of the skull adjacent to the ear canal
Nuclear medicine scan showing increased activity in that same area, consistent with a deep-seated bone infection extending well beyond the ear canal itself

treatment: Harold was admitted for a prolonged course of targeted intravenous antibiotics aimed at the specific bacterium commonly responsible for this condition, alongside strict, closely supervised control of his blood sugar levels, since good sugar control is a key part of recovery from this particular infection. Over the following weeks, his ear pain gradually eased, and the facial weakness stopped progressing further, though it took time to see any real improvement in that.
discharge: He completed a long course of antibiotics as an outpatient, with regular ENT follow-up and repeat scans arranged to confirm the infection was fully clearing, alongside ongoing input from a diabetes specialist team to keep his sugar levels properly controlled going forward.

title: The Sore Throat Two Weeks Ago
personal: Amelia Foster, 7, Female, 122 cm, 24 kg, primary school student. Admitted to the pediatric ward.
incident: About two weeks after having a sore throat that resolved on its own without seeing a doctor, Amelia's mother noticed her face looking puffy around the eyes when she woke up this morning, along with her urine appearing an unusual dark, cola-like color when she used the bathroom. She'd also mentioned a mild headache and seemed a little more tired than usual over the past day or so.
background: Previously a healthy, active child, up to date on immunizations, no known kidney problems before. The sore throat two weeks ago wasn't treated with antibiotics since it seemed to be resolving on its own. No rash, no joint pains.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Amelia was alert and interactive, with mild puffiness noted around both eyes, a blood pressure notably elevated for her age, and a normal temperature.

exam.title: Cardiovascular/Fluid status
exam.body: Mild swelling was also noted over both ankles, and her blood pressure, checked carefully with an appropriately sized cuff, was clearly above what would be expected for a child her age.

exam.title: Skin/Joints
exam.body: No rash anywhere on her body and no joint swelling or tenderness — findings that helped steer the picture away from a different condition that can also follow a sore throat or cause similar kidney symptoms.

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Urinalysis: blood and protein both present
Kidney function: mildly impaired compared with what would be expected for her age
Blood test for recent streptococcal infection: positive
A specific immune marker (complement): reduced, a pattern fitting well with this particular kidney condition

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An ultrasound of her kidneys was arranged:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Both kidneys: mildly enlarged in appearance, otherwise structurally normal
No blockage or other structural abnormality identified

treatment: Amelia was monitored closely with regular blood pressure checks and fluid balance monitoring, with her salt and fluid intake temporarily restricted and a medication given to help control her elevated blood pressure. Over the following week, her blood pressure gradually settled toward normal, the puffiness around her eyes reduced, and her urine slowly returned to its usual color.
discharge: She was discharged home with a plan for regular blood pressure and urine checks over the following weeks to make sure everything continued to settle as expected, with the vast majority of children with this condition going on to make a complete recovery.

title: Not Due for Another Week
personal: Grace Ellison, 24, Female, 163 cm, 58 kg, primary school teacher. Admitted to the gynecology assessment unit.
incident: While getting ready for bed, Grace felt a sudden, sharp pain low on her right side that made her sit down abruptly, followed over the next hour by a dull, persistent ache that spread more generally across her lower abdomen. She felt a little lightheaded standing up to get a glass of water, and noticed some spotting when she went to the bathroom, despite not being due for her period for another week or so.
background: Regular menstrual cycles, mid-cycle at the time judging by her last period, no known ovarian cysts previously diagnosed, currently not using any hormonal contraception, in a stable relationship with consistent condom use, no fever, no prior episodes quite like this.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Grace was mildly anxious, otherwise stable, her blood pressure and heart rate only slightly affected by the pain, temperature normal.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: Tenderness was found low on the right side, without rigidity or significant guarding, and no rebound tenderness that would suggest a more advanced surgical problem.

exam.title: Pelvic, chaperoned
exam.body: Mild tenderness on the right side on examination, no cervical motion tenderness, and no mass or significant swelling felt on either side.

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Urine and serum β-hCG: both negative
Hemoglobin: within normal range, reassuring against any significant ongoing blood loss
White cell count and CRP: normal

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An ultrasound of her pelvis was arranged:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A small amount of free fluid noted in the pelvis, consistent with recent rupture of a small cyst
Right ovary: a small residual cyst visible, otherwise structurally normal with good blood flow on Doppler
No adnexal mass identified
Uterus: normal, confirming the pregnancy test result

treatment: Given how stable Grace remained throughout, with no ongoing signs of significant internal bleeding, the team managed her conservatively with pain relief and a period of observation rather than surgery, checking her blood pressure and pain levels regularly over the following hours to make sure nothing changed. Her pain gradually settled with simple pain relief over the following day.
discharge: She was discharged home the same day with pain relief to continue as needed, reassurance that this kind of event is common and usually resolves on its own without any lasting effect on her fertility, and advice to come back promptly if the pain worsened or she felt increasingly unwell.

title: Dark as Weak Tea
personal: Vanessa Cole, 29, Female, 167 cm, 60 kg, paralegal. Admitted to the acute medical unit.
incident: For the past two days Vanessa has had severe, generalized abdominal pain that doesn't seem to settle in any one place, unlike anything she's experienced before, along with nausea, vomiting, and constipation. Overnight she became noticeably more agitated and confused, at one point crying uncontrollably for no clear reason and rambling in a way that alarmed her partner, who also noticed her urine had looked strangely dark, almost like weak tea, when she'd used the bathroom that morning.
background: She started a new hormonal contraceptive pill about three weeks ago, and has had a couple of previous unexplained episodes of bad abdominal pain over the past two years that were investigated without ever finding a clear cause and eventually settled on their own. No other significant past medical history, no known family history she's aware of, though she mentions an aunt who had "some kind of nerve problem" that was never fully explained.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Vanessa was agitated and intermittently tearful, otherwise not looking acutely unwell in the way her pain might suggest. Temperature normal, heart rate 118, blood pressure notably elevated at 152 over 98.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: There was generalized tenderness without any specific area standing out more than another, no guarding, no rigidity, and bowel sounds present though reduced — findings that didn't fit neatly with a specific surgical cause for her pain despite how severe it was.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: Mild weakness was noted in both hands when tested carefully, something she hadn't mentioned herself, along with brisk reflexes throughout.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Initial routine blood tests and imaging were largely unremarkable, which itself became an important clue, prompting the team to send a more specific urine test:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Routine blood count, kidney and liver function: essentially normal, arguing against several of the more common explanations
Sodium: mildly low
Urine sample left standing exposed to light: darkened noticeably over the course of the day, a distinctive and specific observation

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Urine porphobilinogen: markedly elevated, confirming the specific metabolic problem responsible for her symptoms

treatment: Vanessa's new hormonal contraceptive pill, a known trigger for this particular condition, was stopped immediately, and she was started on a specific intravenous treatment aimed at correcting the underlying metabolic problem, alongside strong pain relief and close monitoring of her heart rate, blood pressure, and neurological function given the risk of this condition affecting the nerves more seriously if not treated promptly. Over the following days, her abdominal pain gradually eased, her agitation and confusion settled, and the weakness in her hands stopped progressing.
discharge: She was discharged with a detailed list of medications and triggers to avoid going forward, a referral to a specialist metabolic team for long-term management and genetic counseling, and a suggestion that her aunt's unexplained "nerve problem" might be worth looking into given how these conditions can run in families.

title: Hotter Than the Flu Should Feel
personal: Diane Foss, 52, Female, 158 cm, 55 kg, restaurant manager. Admitted to the intensive care unit.
incident: Over the past ten days she'd had a mild flu-like illness with a sore throat and cough that she'd been trying to push through at work. Yesterday things took a dramatic turn — a racing heartbeat, drenching sweats, and a fever that climbed steadily through the evening despite paracetamol. This morning her husband found her agitated, trembling, and talking in a way that didn't quite make sense, and by the time they reached the hospital she was vomiting repeatedly and seemed increasingly disoriented.
background: On further questioning, she recalled feeling unusually hot and sweaty for months before this, along with unintentional weight loss and a noticeable tremor in her hands that she'd blamed on stress and too much coffee, never having it checked out. No previously diagnosed thyroid problem, no regular medications, no known allergies.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Diane was agitated and sweating profusely, temperature 40.2°C, heart rate 148 and irregular, blood pressure 160 over 70, with a visible tremor in both outstretched hands.

exam.title: Neck
exam.body: A diffusely enlarged, non-tender thyroid gland was felt, with a faint bruit audible over it.

exam.title: Cardiovascular
exam.body: Rapid, irregular heart rhythm, no murmurs, warm and moist skin throughout.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: Agitated and confused, unable to answer orientation questions correctly, though moving all limbs normally with no focal weakness.

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: TSH: markedly suppressed
Free T4 and Free T3: both very significantly elevated
White cell count: mildly raised, in keeping with the preceding viral illness rather than a serious bacterial infection
Blood cultures: sent

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: A chest X-ray was taken to look for a source of infection given her fever:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Lungs clear, no focal infection identified

treatment: Diane was started immediately on a combination of medications to bring her body's overdrive under control and slow her racing heart, along with cooling measures, fluids, and treatment for the underlying viral illness that appeared to have tipped things over. Over the following 24 hours, her heart rate and temperature gradually came down, and her confusion cleared as she became noticeably calmer and more like herself.
discharge: She was discharged once stable on ongoing thyroid-suppressing medication, with an urgent referral to an endocrinologist to formally diagnose and manage the underlying thyroid condition that had gone unchecked for months before this crisis.

title: Sitting on a Numb Saddle
personal: Patrick Doyle, 45, Male, 180 cm, 92 kg, construction site manager. Admitted to the spinal surgery ward via the emergency department.
incident: He'd had lower back pain radiating down both legs for about a week following some heavy lifting at work, managed with over-the-counter painkillers. This morning, though, things changed dramatically — he found he couldn't feel himself passing urine and, worryingly, hadn't noticed he needed to go until his bladder was uncomfortably full, and he described a strange numbness "like sitting on a numb saddle" spreading across his inner thighs and backside.
background: No previous back surgery, occasional mild back pain over the years managed without medical input, no known bladder or bowel problems before this week, physically active job involving regular heavy lifting.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Patrick was visibly anxious, otherwise well, with normal vital signs.

exam.title: Neurological — lower limbs
exam.body: Mild weakness was noted in both legs, more pronounced in the muscles that lift the foot upward, with reduced reflexes at both ankles.

exam.title: Sensory/saddle area
exam.body: Reduced sensation to light touch was found across the inner thighs, buttocks, and perianal area on both sides in a pattern doctors specifically call the "saddle" distribution, along with reduced tone felt on a gentle rectal examination performed with his consent.

exam.title: Bladder
exam.body: A bladder scan performed at the bedside showed a significantly larger than expected volume of retained urine, consistent with his own description of reduced sensation when urinating.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An urgent MRI scan of his lower spine was arranged, given how time-critical this diagnosis is for preventing permanent damage:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A large disc herniation compressing the nerve roots at the lower part of his spinal canal, consistent with the clinical findings

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Full blood count and inflammatory markers: normal, arguing against an infective cause

treatment: Patrick was taken to theatre within hours for emergency spinal surgery, since the timing of surgery has a real bearing on how much function can be recovered. His bladder sensation and leg strength began showing small signs of improvement over the following days, monitored closely by the spinal and urology teams together.
discharge: He was discharged to continue his recovery with physiotherapy and close urology follow-up given the bladder symptoms, with the team explaining honestly that some symptoms might take months to improve fully, or in a minority of cases might not resolve completely, while remaining encouraged by his early progress.

title: The Tooth He Kept Putting Off
personal: Marcus Bell, 38, Male, 178 cm, 88 kg, plumber. Admitted to the ENT/maxillofacial ward via the emergency department.
incident: For the past four days he'd had a painful, swollen lower molar tooth that he'd been meaning to get looked at but kept putting off given work commitments. Over the past 24 hours, the swelling had spread rapidly beneath his jaw and down into his neck, becoming increasingly firm and painful, and this evening he'd started drooling because swallowing had become too painful and difficult, with his voice sounding muffled and different to his wife.
background: Poor dental hygiene by his own admission, hasn't seen a dentist in several years, no known allergies, no diabetes or other significant medical history, no previous episodes like this.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Marcus was anxious and drooling, sitting forward and leaning slightly to keep his airway comfortable. Temperature 38.8°C, heart rate 112, breathing slightly labored.

exam.title: Head and neck
exam.body: Firm, board-like swelling was felt across the floor of his mouth and both sides beneath his jaw, extending down into his upper neck, with his tongue pushed upward and backward in his mouth by the swelling underneath it. The skin over the swelling was tense, red, and exquisitely tender.

exam.title: Airway
exam.body: His voice had a muffled, "hot potato" quality, and mild stridor could be heard, prompting the team to treat his airway as a priority above all else.

investigations.title: Airway
investigations.body: Given the airway concern, the priority was securing his airway safely with an anesthetist present before pursuing detailed imaging:

reports.title: Airway Assessment Report
lines: Direct visualization confirmed significant swelling of the floor of the mouth pushing the tongue backward, with a safe airway secured under controlled conditions

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: Once his airway was secured, a CT scan of his neck was performed:

reports.title: Imaging Report
