personal: Margaret Ellwood, 82, Female, 158 cm, 60 kg, retired seamstress. Seen in the memory assessment clinic.
incident: Her daughter has noticed a gradual change over the past two years — Margaret repeating the same questions and stories multiple times within a single conversation, misplacing everyday items in odd places like finding her keys in the refrigerator, and more recently getting lost trying to find her way home from a route she's walked for decades. Today's visit was prompted by an episode last week where she left the stove on and forgot she'd been cooking.
background: No significant past medical history apart from well-controlled high blood pressure, no history of stroke, no recent illness, lives alone though her daughter has become increasingly concerned about her safety. No family history of early-onset memory problems, though her own mother had "confusion" in her final years.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Margaret was pleasant and cooperative, alert, with normal vital signs and no signs of acute illness.

exam.title: Neurological/Cognitive
exam.body: Formal memory testing showed clear difficulty recalling a short list of words after a delay, and some difficulty with tasks requiring planning and orientation to the exact date, though her language and social skills remained relatively well preserved. No focal weakness, normal gait.

exam.title: General, further
exam.body: No evidence of an acute confusional state — she was calm, consistent, and her difficulties had clearly been present and slowly worsening over a long period rather than appearing suddenly.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood tests were sent to look for reversible causes of memory problems:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Thyroid function, vitamin B12, and folate levels: all normal, arguing against a reversible metabolic cause
Kidney and liver function: normal

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An MRI scan of her brain was arranged:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Generalized shrinkage of brain tissue, more pronounced in areas involved with memory, without the pattern of small strokes or significant blood vessel damage that would point toward a different type of dementia

treatment: Margaret was started on a medication aimed at supporting her remaining memory function for as long as possible, alongside practical support put in place at home, including a referral to social services to arrange help with daily tasks and safety measures like a stove timer. Her family was given detailed information and support resources to help them plan for her ongoing care.
discharge: She was discharged home with regular follow-up arranged through the memory clinic to monitor her progress, and her daughter was connected with a local carers' support group to help navigate the road ahead.

title: Smaller Handwriting
personal: Albert Finch, 68, Male, 175 cm, 80 kg, retired postal worker. Seen in the neurology outpatient clinic.
incident: Over the past eight months, Albert's wife has noticed a subtle tremor develop in his right hand, most obvious when he's sitting still watching television and disappearing when he reaches for something, along with his handwriting becoming smaller and more cramped than it used to be. More recently, she's noticed he walks with a stooped posture, taking smaller, shuffling steps, and his face seems to show less expression than it used to, something a friend even commented on at a family gathering.
background: No significant past medical history, no family history of similar tremors, no exposure to particular toxins or medications known to cause tremor, no recent strokes, still working part-time in the garden though he's noticed it takes him longer to complete tasks he used to do quickly.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Albert was otherwise well, with normal vital signs and notably reduced facial expression during the conversation.

exam.title: Neurological — motor
exam.body: A resting tremor was observed in his right hand, most prominent when his hand was still and reducing with purposeful movement, along with increased resistance felt when the doctor moved his arm passively through its range of motion — a specific quality doctors describe as "cogwheel" in nature. His movements overall were slower than expected for his age.

exam.title: Gait
exam.body: He walked with a stooped posture, small shuffling steps, and reduced arm swing on the right side compared with the left, with some difficulty initiating his first steps from standing still.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: Given how classic his combination of findings was, the diagnosis was largely made on examination alone, but an MRI scan of his brain was arranged to check for other causes:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: No evidence of small strokes or fluid buildup within the brain that might explain his symptoms through a different mechanism, supporting the clinical diagnosis

investigations.title: Treatment Response
investigations.body: A trial of a specific medication was used partly as a diagnostic tool, since a strong response supports this particular diagnosis:

reports.title: Treatment Response Report
lines: A noticeable improvement in his tremor and stiffness was observed after starting the medication, further supporting the suspected diagnosis

treatment: Albert was started on medication to ease his symptoms, along with a referral to physiotherapy to help maintain his mobility and balance. Over the following weeks, his tremor became less noticeable and his movements grew a little quicker and easier.
discharge: He continued regular follow-up with the neurology team to adjust his medication over time as needed, along with ongoing physiotherapy input, and information for both him and his wife about the condition and what to expect going forward.

title: Ten Minutes Before It Loosens Up
personal: Diane Whitmore, 63, Female, 163 cm, 78 kg, retired shop assistant. Seen in the orthopedic outpatient clinic.
incident: Over the past two years, Diane has noticed a gradually worsening ache in her right knee, particularly after standing for long periods or climbing stairs, which has slowly gotten to the point where she now feels stiff for a good ten minutes after getting up in the morning before it loosens up. She's noticed some swelling around the knee at times, though nothing that's ever been hot or dramatically painful, and lately she's had to give up her regular walking group because of it.
background: Overweight for many years, worked for decades in a job requiring long periods of standing, no previous knee injuries that she recalls, no family history of inflammatory joint disease, generally well otherwise.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Diane was otherwise well, with no fever and normal vital signs.

exam.title: Joint examination
exam.body: The right knee showed mild swelling and a bony, firm enlargement felt along the joint margins, with a coarse grating sensation felt when the knee was bent and straightened, and a modestly reduced range of motion compared with the left knee. The joint was not particularly warm or red, and there was no significant tenderness to light touch, distinguishing it from a more inflammatory or infective process.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An X-ray of both knees was taken for comparison:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Right knee: narrowing of the joint space, bony spurs at the joint margins, and increased density of the bone just beneath the joint surface — a combination of findings characteristic of this condition
Left knee: much milder changes of the same type

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to help rule out an inflammatory cause:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Inflammatory markers (ESR and CRP): normal
A specific antibody test associated with a different type of joint disease: negative

treatment: Diane was started on a structured plan including physiotherapy to strengthen the muscles supporting her knee, weight management advice, and simple pain relief for flare-ups, with an injection into the joint offered for more significant symptom relief in the meantime. Over the following months, her pain became more manageable with these measures, allowing her to gradually return to some gentle walking.
discharge: She continued with physiotherapy and weight management support long-term, with a discussion about the possibility of knee replacement surgery down the line if her symptoms significantly worsened or stopped responding to these more conservative measures.

title: Stiff for an Hour Every Morning
personal: Angela Foster, 41, Female, 165 cm, 68 kg, office administrator. Seen in the rheumatology outpatient clinic.
incident: Over the past three months, Angela has developed pain, swelling, and stiffness in the small joints of both hands, along with similar symptoms in both wrists, noticing the stiffness is particularly bad in the mornings, lasting well over an hour before easing. The symptoms have been symmetrical, affecting both sides of her body similarly, and she's also felt generally more tired than usual and has lost her appetite somewhat over this time.
background: No previous joint problems, no family history of rheumatoid arthritis though an aunt has "some kind of autoimmune thing," non-smoker, no recent infections that might explain a reactive joint problem, no psoriasis or skin changes.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Angela was otherwise well, mildly fatigued-looking, with normal vital signs.

exam.title: Joint examination
exam.body: Several of the small joints in both hands, particularly at the base of her fingers and her wrists, were swollen, warm, and tender, symmetrically affecting both sides, with a soft, boggy quality to the swelling rather than the bony firmness seen in a different, more wear-and-tear type of joint problem.

exam.title: Skin/General
exam.body: No psoriasis patches on her skin or nails, no rash on her face, no mouth ulcers.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to look for specific antibodies and markers of inflammation:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Rheumatoid factor: positive
A more specific antibody test (anti-CCP): also positive
Inflammatory markers (ESR and CRP): both elevated
A specific antibody test associated with lupus: negative

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: X-rays of both hands were taken:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: Early signs of narrowing at several of the small joint spaces and mild soft tissue swelling, without established bony damage yet, consistent with an early stage of this condition

treatment: Angela was started on a long-term medication, alongside a short course of steroids to bring the current flare under control more quickly, and close monitoring for how well she tolerated the medication. Over the following weeks, her joint swelling and morning stiffness gradually improved.
discharge: She continued regular follow-up with the rheumatology team to monitor her response to treatment and adjust medications as needed, with blood tests arranged periodically to check both her disease activity and for any medication side effects.

title: Triggered by Rolling Over
personal: Susan Naylor, 58, Female, 162 cm, 70 kg, retired administrator. Seen in the emergency department.
incident: For the past two days, Susan has experienced sudden, intense spinning sensations lasting less than a minute each time, specifically triggered by rolling over in bed or looking up to a high shelf, with the room seeming to spin violently around her before settling back to normal. Between episodes she feels completely well, though she's become increasingly anxious about moving her head at all for fear of triggering another attack.
background: No previous episodes like this, no recent head injury, no hearing loss or ringing in her ears, no headache, no known cardiovascular problems, no recent illness.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Susan was well between episodes, with normal vital signs and no signs of acute distress at rest.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: Normal strength, sensation, and coordination throughout, no slurred speech, no facial weakness — findings that argued strongly against a stroke as the cause.

exam.title: Specific positional testing
exam.body: A maneuver was performed that involved moving Susan's head into a specific position known to trigger this condition, and it reproduced her exact spinning sensation along with a characteristic pattern of eye movement (nystagmus) that doctors specifically look for, which settled within less than a minute.

investigations.title: Clinical
investigations.body: The diagnosis was made through the specific positional testing described above, rather than blood tests or imaging, given how classic and reproducible the trigger and pattern were:

reports.title: Clinical Assessment Report
lines: Positive positional test reproducing the exact symptom and a specific, brief eye movement pattern strongly characteristic of this diagnosis, with no features suggesting a more serious central cause

investigations.title: Hearing
investigations.body: Given the entirely normal neurological examination, no imaging was felt to be needed, but a hearing check was offered:

reports.title: Hearing Assessment
lines: Normal hearing in both ears, arguing against a different inner ear condition sometimes confused with this one

treatment: Susan was taught and guided through a specific series of head movements, performed right there in the department, designed to settle her symptoms. Her symptoms noticeably improved even during the session, and she was given instructions to repeat a simpler version of the exercise at home if needed.
discharge: She was discharged with written instructions for the head-repositioning exercise to use if symptoms recurred, along with reassurance about the generally short-lived and treatable nature of this condition, and advice to return if anything different or more concerning developed, such as hearing changes or persistent imbalance.

title: Six Times a Day
personal: Liam Brennan, 24, Male, 178 cm, 68 kg (recent weight loss), graduate student. Admitted to the gastroenterology ward.
incident: For the past three months, Liam has had recurring crampy abdominal pain, mostly on his right lower side, along with episodes of watery diarrhea, sometimes six or more times a day, and over this time he's lost a noticeable amount of weight without trying to. Over the past week, things have worsened, with a persistent low-grade fever and increasing fatigue, and today he noticed a small amount of blood mixed into his stool for the first time.
background: No previous bowel problems diagnosed, though he mentions occasional "stomach trouble" over the years that never seemed serious enough to investigate. A cousin has ulcerative colitis, non-smoker, no recent travel or antibiotic use that might explain an infectious cause, mouth ulcers on and off for the past few months that he'd assumed were just stress-related.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Liam was thin, tired-looking, temperature 38.0°C, heart rate 96, mild pallor.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: Tenderness was found in the right lower abdomen, with a vague sense of fullness felt on deeper palpation in that area, without the same rigid guarding that would be expected with a different, more acute surgical emergency.

exam.title: Mouth/Skin
exam.body: A couple of small ulcers were seen inside his mouth, and mild tenderness with a small area of redness was noted over his shin — a skin finding sometimes associated with this bowel condition.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood and stool samples were sent:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Hemoglobin: mildly low
Inflammatory markers (CRP and ESR): both elevated
Stool tests for infectious causes: negative
A specific stool marker of bowel inflammation (fecal calprotectin): markedly elevated

investigations.title: Endoscopy
investigations.body: A colonoscopy with biopsies was arranged to look directly at the bowel lining:

reports.title: Endoscopy Report
lines: Patchy areas of inflammation seen throughout parts of the large bowel with normal-looking bowel in between affected areas, rather than one continuous stretch of inflammation
Biopsies confirmed a pattern of inflammation extending through the full thickness of the bowel wall, both findings supporting one particular type of inflammatory bowel disease over the other

treatment: Liam was started on steroids to bring the current flare under control, along with nutritional support given his weight loss, and the gastroenterology team began planning a longer-term medication to keep the condition in remission going forward. Over the following two weeks, his diarrhea frequency reduced, his energy began to improve, and the fever settled.
discharge: He was discharged on a tapering course of steroids alongside a new long-term medication to maintain remission, with regular gastroenterology follow-up arranged, dietary advice, and information about support resources for people living with this lifelong condition.

title: More Than Just Weight Gain
personal: Terrence Wallace, 50, Male, 176 cm, 82 kg, self-employed contractor. Admitted to the gastroenterology/liver ward.
incident: Over the past two weeks, Terrence has felt increasingly unwell, with a poor appetite, nausea, and a dull ache in his upper right abdomen, and over the past few days his wife has noticed his eyes and skin taking on a yellow tinge. Today he developed a fever, and his abdomen appears more swollen and rounder than usual, something his wife first noticed about a week ago and assumed was just weight gain.
background: A long history of heavy daily alcohol use for over twenty years, admits to drinking even more than usual over the past month due to stress. No known prior liver diagnosis, though he recalls being told his liver blood tests were "a bit off" a couple of years ago. No viral hepatitis risk factors that he's aware of, no other significant medical history.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Terrence was jaundiced and unwell-looking, temperature 38.2°C, heart rate 102, mildly confused when asked more complex questions.

exam.title: Abdominal
exam.body: His abdomen was visibly distended with a fluid wave felt on examination, consistent with fluid accumulation, and his liver felt enlarged and tender just below the right ribs.

exam.title: Skin/General
exam.body: Spider-like small blood vessels were seen on his chest, and his palms appeared unusually red — both changes doctors specifically associate with longstanding liver strain.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent to check his liver function in detail:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Bilirubin: markedly elevated
Liver enzymes: elevated, with a specific pattern and ratio between two of them typically seen with alcohol-related liver damage rather than other causes
Clotting function: impaired, reflecting how much strain his liver was under
Viral hepatitis screening: negative

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An ultrasound of his abdomen was arranged:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: An enlarged, fatty-appearing liver with fluid visible in the abdominal cavity
No gallstones or blockage of the bile ducts seen
No mass identified within the liver

treatment: Terrence was admitted for supportive care including nutritional support, careful management of the fluid building up in his abdomen, and a specific medication considered for more severe cases, alongside close monitoring for signs of his liver function declining further. Over the following two weeks, his jaundice gradually began to improve and his confusion cleared.
discharge: He was discharged with a strong recommendation and referral for alcohol treatment support services, close follow-up with the liver team to monitor his ongoing liver function, and a frank conversation about the importance of stopping alcohol completely to give his liver the best chance of recovering.

title: Spots in Her Vision
personal: Danielle Reyes, 29, Female, 165 cm, 82 kg (pregnant, 34 weeks gestation), first pregnancy. Admitted to the maternity assessment unit.
incident: Over the past few days, Danielle has noticed a persistent headache that won't fully go away with paracetamol, along with some blurring and occasional "spots" in her vision. Today she noticed her hands and face looked more swollen than usual when she looked in the mirror, and she mentioned a dull ache just under her right ribs that she hadn't had before.
background: First pregnancy, otherwise healthy before becoming pregnant. Blood pressure readings had been creeping up slightly at her last two antenatal visits, though still within a borderline range that wasn't flagged as urgent at the time. No known kidney problems, no family history of similar pregnancy complications that she's aware of.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Danielle was alert but uncomfortable. Blood pressure 162 over 104 (notably high), mild swelling noted around her face and hands.

exam.title: Abdominal/Obstetric
exam.body: Tenderness was found just under the right ribs, her uterus was soft between contractions with no localized rigidity, and the baby's movements felt normal to her.

exam.title: Fetal assessment
exam.body: A continuous fetal heart trace showed a reassuring, normal pattern throughout the monitoring period.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: Brisk reflexes were noted at both knees, though no other neurological abnormalities were found.

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio: significantly elevated, indicating protein leaking into her urine
Liver function tests: mildly elevated
Platelet count: mildly reduced from her earlier pregnancy readings
Kidney function: mildly impaired compared with her booking bloods

investigations.title: Monitoring
investigations.body: Given the persistent headache and visual symptoms, close monitoring of her blood pressure and symptoms was continued alongside the blood work:

reports.title: Monitoring Report
lines: Repeated blood pressure readings remained persistently elevated despite rest, and her headache and visual disturbance continued throughout observation

treatment: Danielle was started on medication to bring her blood pressure down to a safer range, along with a course of medication to help protect the baby's lungs in case early delivery became necessary, and a further medication was given to reduce her risk of a seizure. She was monitored extremely closely, and given the severity of her symptoms and blood results, the team proceeded with an induced delivery earlier than her due date once she and the baby were both considered stable enough for it.
discharge: Both Danielle and her baby did well following the delivery, with her blood pressure gradually returning toward normal over the following weeks under close monitoring, and she was counselled about her increased risk of this condition in any future pregnancy and the importance of early antenatal blood pressure checks.

title: Stopped Taking the Tablets
personal: Victor Abara, 54, Male, 178 cm, 92 kg, taxi company owner. Admitted to the acute medical unit.
incident: For the past few hours, Victor has had a severe, pounding headache along with blurred vision, and his wife noticed he seemed increasingly confused and unsteady when he tried to walk to the car. He mentioned some chest tightness and a sensation of his heart pounding hard in his chest, and felt increasingly short of breath on the way to the hospital.
background: Known high blood pressure for over ten years, admits he stopped taking his tablets several months ago after running out and not getting around to a refill. No known kidney disease previously diagnosed, no chest pain history, no recreational drug use.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Victor was anxious and mildly confused. Blood pressure 224 over 132 (severely elevated), heart rate 104, respiratory rate 22.

exam.title: Neurological
exam.body: Mildly confused but no focal weakness, no facial droop, pupils equal and reactive, no neck stiffness.

exam.title: Eye examination
exam.body: Examining the back of his eyes revealed swelling of the optic nerve and small areas of bleeding within the retina — changes doctors specifically associate with severely elevated blood pressure affecting the eyes.

exam.title: Cardiovascular/Respiratory
exam.body: Fine crackles were heard at the bases of both lungs, and a soft murmur was noted, suggesting his heart was under significant strain from the high pressure it had been working against.

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Kidney function: significantly impaired compared to what would be expected
Urinalysis: protein and blood both present
Troponin: mildly elevated, suggesting some strain on the heart

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: CT head: no bleeding, no stroke identified
Chest X-ray: mild fluid at the base of both lungs, consistent with the heart struggling under the pressure load

treatment: Victor was started on intravenous medication to bring his blood pressure down in a careful, controlled manner rather than too quickly, which can itself be dangerous, with close monitoring of his blood pressure, kidney function, and neurological state throughout. Over the following 24 hours, his blood pressure gradually came down to a safer range, his confusion cleared, and his breathing eased.
discharge: He was discharged on a combination of blood pressure medications with a clear plan and reminders in place to ensure he never runs out again, along with close follow-up with his regular doctor to monitor his kidney function and blood pressure control going forward.

title: Worse After Getting Better
personal: Melissa Grant, 38, Female, 165 cm, 70 kg, HR consultant. Seen in outpatient clinic.
incident: About ten days ago, Melissa had what seemed like an ordinary head cold, with a runny nose and mild congestion that she expected to clear up within a week as usual. Instead, over the past four days, things have worsened rather than improved — a constant, throbbing pressure has developed across her forehead and cheeks, worse when she bends forward, along with thick yellow-green discharge from her nose and a mild fever that's come on in just the past two days.
background: No history of chronic sinus problems, no known nasal polyps or allergies, non-smoker, no recent dental problems, no previous similar prolonged illness.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Melissa was mildly unwell, temperature 38.1°C, otherwise stable.

exam.title: Head and face
exam.body: Tenderness was found over both cheekbones and the forehead when gently pressed, worse on the right side, and bending her head forward clearly worsened the pressure sensation she described.

exam.title: ENT
exam.body: Thick, discolored discharge was seen at the back of her nasal passages, with mild redness and swelling of the lining inside her nose.

investigations.title: Clinical
investigations.body: Given how classic the pattern and duration of her symptoms were — worsening after an initial period of improvement, a hallmark doctors specifically look for — the diagnosis was made clinically without needing imaging:

reports.title: Clinical Assessment Report
lines: Symptoms lasting beyond ten days with a "double-worsening" pattern (initial improvement followed by a clear deterioration), combined with facial tenderness and thick discolored discharge, supporting a bacterial rather than purely viral cause

investigations.title: Observation
investigations.body: Routine observations were checked to make sure nothing more serious was developing:

reports.title: Observation Report
lines: No signs of the infection spreading toward the eye or more deeply into the skull, such as swelling around the eye or worsening neurological symptoms

treatment: Melissa was started on a course of antibiotics along with a nasal spray to help reduce the swelling inside her nose and improve drainage, plus simple pain relief for the facial pressure and headache. Over the following week, the facial pain gradually eased and the discharge became clearer and less frequent.
discharge: She completed her course of antibiotics with symptoms fully resolved, and was advised to return if symptoms like this recurred frequently, since that might warrant a closer look at any underlying structural cause within her sinuses.

title: Eyelashes Stuck Together
personal: Mia Foster, 6, Female, 118 cm, 21 kg, primary school student. Seen in the pediatric assessment unit.
incident: Yesterday evening, Mia's mother noticed her right eye looked a little pink and watery, which she assumed was from rubbing it too much. This morning, though, Mia woke up with her eyelashes stuck together with thick, yellow discharge that had crusted overnight, and by midday her left eye had started looking similarly red and irritated too.
background: No known eye problems before, no allergies. A couple of children at her school have had "pink eye" recently, no recent injury to the eye, no contact lens use.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Mia was otherwise well, no fever, playful and interactive.

exam.title: Eye examination
exam.body: Both eyes showed redness of the white part of the eye and the inner eyelid surface, with thick, yellow-white discharge visibly crusted along the eyelashes of the right eye more than the left, and no swelling extending beyond the eyelid itself onto the surrounding skin or face.

exam.title: Vision/General
exam.body: Her vision appeared normal on simple testing appropriate for her age, no pain with eye movement, and no sensitivity to light.

investigations.title: Clinical
investigations.body: The diagnosis was made clinically based on the characteristic thick, sticky discharge and appearance, without needing a swab in this straightforward case:

reports.title: Clinical Assessment Report
lines: Thick, purulent discharge with crusting, spreading from one eye to the other over about a day, a pattern more typical of a bacterial rather than viral or allergic cause

investigations.title: Assessment
investigations.body: Given no swelling extended beyond the eyelid, no further imaging or blood tests were felt necessary, but the surrounding skin and eye socket were checked carefully:

reports.title: Assessment Report
lines: No swelling, redness, or tenderness of the skin around the eye socket, no restriction of eye movement, arguing against a more serious infection spreading behind the eye

treatment: Mia was started on medicated eye drops, along with advice on gently cleaning away the crusted discharge with cooled boiled water and a clean cloth before each application, and careful handwashing to avoid spreading it to family members. Within two days, the redness and discharge had noticeably improved.
discharge: She completed her course of eye drops with both eyes fully settled, and was kept off school until the discharge had cleared, in line with usual school policy for this kind of contagious eye infection.

title: Worried About His Heart
personal: Kevin Marsh, 26, Male, 180 cm, 76 kg, graphic designer. Seen in the emergency department.
incident: For the past three days, Kevin has had a sharp, aching pain on the left side of his chest, worse when he takes a deep breath, coughs, or presses on the area himself, which has made him increasingly anxious given how often chest pain is talked about as a warning sign. The pain doesn't radiate anywhere else, and he hasn't had any breathlessness, sweating, or dizziness alongside it, though he admits he's been unable to stop worrying about his heart since it started.
background: No significant past medical history, non-smoker, no family history of early heart disease. Recently started a new home workout routine involving push-ups and weights that he'd not done in a long while, no recent injury or trauma to the chest.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Kevin was anxious but otherwise well, with normal vital signs and no distress at rest.

exam.title: Chest wall examination
exam.body: Pressing directly over several of the joints where his ribs meet his breastbone reproduced his exact pain precisely, with the pain also worsened by certain arm movements and deep breathing, but with no pain at rest when left untouched.

exam.title: Cardiovascular/Respiratory
exam.body: Heart sounds normal, no murmurs, no friction rub, chest clear with equal air entry on both sides, no calf swelling or tenderness.

investigations.title: ECG
investigations.body: Given his age, the reproducible nature of the pain on direct pressure, and the absence of any concerning features, the priority was simply to rule out a cardiac cause given how anxious he was about it:

reports.title: ECG Report
lines: Normal electrical activity of the heart, no signs of strain or a heart attack

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Blood was sent as a reassuring step given his anxiety about a heart cause:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Troponin: normal
D-dimer: not needed given the low likelihood of a clot based on his risk factors and findings

treatment: Kevin was reassured about the benign nature of the diagnosis, given his heart tests were entirely normal, and was advised to take a simple anti-inflammatory medication along with resting from the new exercise routine that had likely triggered it. Over the following week to two, the pain gradually settled as he eased back into activity more gradually.
discharge: He was discharged with reassurance and written information explaining why his heart tests ruled out anything serious, along with advice on gradually reintroducing exercise and returning if the pain changed character or new symptoms developed.

title: Hours in the Pool
personal: Sarah Kim, 27, Female, 163 cm, 58 kg, swim instructor. Seen in urgent care clinic.
incident: Over the past two days, Sarah has had increasing pain and itching in her right ear, made worse whenever she tugs gently on her earlobe or chews food, along with a sensation of fullness and slightly reduced hearing on that side. She spends several hours a day in the pool for work and can't recall the last time her ears felt properly dry.
background: No previous ear infections of this type, no known allergies, no recent air travel, no discharge noticed until today when she saw a small amount of clear fluid on her pillow.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Sarah was otherwise well, afebrile, no signs of feeling generally unwell.

exam.title: Ear examination
exam.body: Gently pulling on the outer ear and pressing on the small bump in front of it both reproduced sharp pain, the ear canal itself appeared red, swollen, and narrowed with a small amount of clear discharge, and the eardrum, though difficult to see clearly through the swelling, appeared normal where visible.

exam.title: General, further
exam.body: No swelling or tenderness behind the ear, no facial weakness, blood sugar checked and normal — arguing against the more dangerous, deeper version of this condition sometimes seen in people with diabetes.

investigations.title: Ear Examination
investigations.body: The diagnosis was made through direct examination of the ear canal, without needing blood tests given how classic and localized the findings were:

reports.title: Ear Examination Report
lines: Diffusely red, swollen ear canal with clear discharge and pain on manipulation of the outer ear, typical of inflammation confined to the ear canal itself rather than spreading to deeper structures

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: A swab of the discharge was taken given how much water exposure she has for work:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Swab culture: grew a bacterium commonly associated with this condition, particularly in people with frequent water exposure

treatment: Sarah was started on antibiotic ear drops along with advice to keep the ear completely dry for the next couple of weeks, avoiding swimming and using a hairdryer on a cool setting after showering if needed. Within a few days, the pain and swelling had noticeably improved.
discharge: She completed her course of ear drops with the infection fully settled, and was given practical advice on using earplugs while swimming and thoroughly drying her ears afterward to help prevent this recurring given her job.

title: White Patches
personal: Noah Bailey, 15, Male, 170 cm, 60 kg, high school student. Seen in pediatric assessment unit.
incident: Three days ago Noah developed a sore throat that's steadily worsened, now making it painful to swallow even his own saliva at times, along with a fever and general body aches that have kept him home from school. His mother noticed this morning that his neck felt swollen and tender on both sides, and looking into his throat with a flashlight, she saw white patches on his tonsils that worried her enough to bring him in.
background: No previous tonsil problems, up to date on immunizations, no recent travel. A couple of classmates have had "bad sore throats" recently, no known allergies.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Noah was unwell but alert, temperature 38.9°C, heart rate 100, no drooling, able to swallow fluids with discomfort.

exam.title: ENT
exam.body: Both tonsils were markedly enlarged and red, covered with distinct white-yellow patches of exudate, with tender, swollen lymph nodes felt on both sides of his neck toward the front rather than the back.

exam.title: Abdominal/Skin
exam.body: No enlarged spleen felt on abdominal examination, no rash anywhere on his skin, and his voice, while slightly muffled from the swelling, didn't have the specific "hot potato" quality that would suggest an abscess forming beside the tonsil.

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: A rapid swab test was taken from his throat:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Rapid strep test: positive for the bacterium responsible for bacterial tonsillitis

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: Given mononucleosis was still being considered, a specific blood test was sent as well:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Rapid mononucleosis antibody test: negative, along with a normal-appearing white cell count on the blood film, arguing against that alternative diagnosis

treatment: Noah was started on a course of antibiotics along with pain relief to help him manage the throat discomfort and continue drinking fluids. Within two days, his fever settled and the swallowing pain became much more manageable, and the swelling in his neck gradually reduced.
discharge: He completed his full course of antibiotics at home and was kept off school until he was fever-free and feeling well again, as advised, to avoid passing the infection on to his classmates.

title: Honey-Colored Crust
personal: Chloe Simmons, 4, Female, 102 cm, 16 kg, preschooler. Seen in pediatric assessment unit.
incident: Three days ago Chloe's mother noticed a small, red spot appear near her nose, which she assumed was an insect bite or a scratch from playing outside. Since then, it's grown into a cluster of blisters that quickly burst and have crusted over with a distinctive honey-colored, golden crust, and a few similar new spots have appeared on her chin and upper lip over the past day.
background: Attends preschool, where her mother mentions another child recently had "some kind of skin thing" around the mouth. No known eczema or other skin conditions, no fever, otherwise playing and eating normally.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Chloe was well and playful, afebrile, no signs of feeling unwell in herself.

exam.title: Skin
exam.body: Clusters of shallow, honey-colored crusted lesions were seen around her nose, chin, and upper lip, with a couple of areas showing thin, golden crust flaking at the edges, and no surrounding warmth, swelling, or spreading redness that would suggest a deeper skin infection.

exam.title: General, further
exam.body: No swollen lymph nodes felt in her neck, no lesions found anywhere else on her body away from her face.

investigations.title: Clinical
investigations.body: The diagnosis was made clinically based on the very characteristic honey-colored crusting, without needing a swab in this straightforward case:

reports.title: Clinical Assessment Report
lines: Classic honey-colored, crusted lesions clustered around the nose and mouth, a distribution and appearance specific to this superficial bacterial skin infection rather than a viral cold sore, which typically looks more like small, painful, fluid-filled blisters in a tighter cluster

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: A swab was still taken from one of the lesions to confirm the specific bacterium and guide treatment if needed:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Skin swab: grew a bacterium commonly responsible for this type of skin infection

treatment: Chloe was started on a topical antibiotic cream to apply directly to the affected areas several times a day, along with advice on gently soaking off the crusts with warm water before each application and keeping her fingernails short to reduce the spread from scratching. Within a week, the lesions had fully healed.
discharge: She was kept home from preschool until the lesions had crusted over and started healing, as advised, with hygiene tips given to her mother to reduce the small risk of it spreading to other family members or classmates.

title: Hot Needles Around His Side
personal: Raymond Betts, 64, Male, 174 cm, 79 kg, retired engineer. Seen in outpatient clinic.
incident: Four days ago, Raymond developed a burning, tingling discomfort on the right side of his chest that he initially dismissed as a pulled muscle from gardening. Two days later, a band of small, painful blisters appeared across the same area, wrapping partway around his right side from his spine toward his chest, and the pain has since become sharp and severe, described by him as feeling like "hot needles."
background: Had chickenpox as a child, no known immune problems, generally healthy apart from well-controlled type 2 diabetes. No recent chest trauma or new skin products that might explain a rash, no fever.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Raymond was otherwise well, afebrile, uncomfortable from the pain rather than looking generally unwell.

exam.title: Skin
exam.body: A band of grouped, fluid-filled blisters on a red base was seen wrapping around the right side of his trunk, following a single strip of skin from his back around toward the front, stopping abruptly at the midline — a distribution doctors specifically recognize as following one nerve's territory rather than crossing to the other side of the body.

exam.title: General, further
exam.body: No similar lesions found anywhere else on his body, no eye involvement, no facial weakness.

investigations.title: Clinical
investigations.body: The diagnosis was made clinically based on the very characteristic band-like distribution of the blisters, without needing further testing in this straightforward case:

reports.title: Clinical Assessment Report
lines: Grouped vesicles confined to a single nerve's territory on one side of the body, stopping sharply at the midline, a pattern highly specific to this viral reactivation rather than a skin irritation or allergic cause

investigations.title: Laboratory
investigations.body: A swab from one of the blisters was taken to confirm the specific virus, particularly given his diabetes:

reports.title: Laboratory Report
lines: Swab from a vesicle: confirmed the virus responsible for chickenpox and shingles

treatment: Raymond was started promptly on an antiviral medication in tablet form, given within the window where it works best at reducing the severity and duration of the outbreak, along with pain relief for the nerve pain, which can sometimes be quite severe and slow to settle even after the rash itself heals. Over the following two weeks, the blisters gradually crusted over and the sharp pain slowly began to ease.
discharge: He was advised to keep the area covered while blisters were still present to avoid passing the virus to anyone who'd never had chickenpox, with a follow-up arranged to check on the nerve pain, since it can occasionally persist for some time after the rash has fully healed.

title: Electric Shocks Across Her Face
personal: Patricia Nolan-Wright, 58, Female, 162 cm, 65 kg, retired teacher. Seen in neurology outpatient clinic.
incident: Over the past three months, Patricia has experienced sudden, brief episodes of excruciating, electric shock-like pain shooting through the right side of her face, each lasting only a few seconds but occurring multiple times a day, often triggered by seemingly trivial things like brushing her teeth, a light breeze on her face, or even chewing food. Between episodes she feels completely fine, though she's become increasingly anxious and has started avoiding touching that side of her face altogether, even avoiding certain foods.
background: No previous facial pain like this, no known dental problems on that side (though she's seen a dentist twice about it without any issue found), no recent trauma to her face or head, no known multiple sclerosis or other neurological conditions, otherwise generally healthy.

exam.title: General
exam.body: Patricia was well between episodes, anxious about triggering an attack, with normal vital signs.

exam.title: Neurological — cranial nerves
exam.body: Sensation to light touch on her face was normal on formal testing, with no weakness of her facial muscles, and gently touching a specific small area near her lip reliably triggered a brief jolt of her characteristic pain, which she confirmed matched exactly what she experiences at home.

exam.title: Dental/TMJ
exam.body: Her teeth and jaw joint were examined and found to be entirely normal, with no tenderness, clicking, or dental disease found to explain her pain.

investigations.title: Imaging
investigations.body: An MRI scan of her brain was arranged, partly to look for a specific cause of this condition and partly to rule out an alternative underlying condition:

reports.title: Imaging Report
lines: A blood vessel identified sitting in close contact with the nerve responsible for facial sensation on the right side, a finding commonly associated with this type of facial pain
No areas of damage elsewhere in the brain that would suggest a different underlying neurological condition

investigations.title: Clinical
investigations.body: Given the very classic history and trigger pattern, along with the reassuring scan, no further testing was felt necessary:

reports.title: Clinical Assessment Report
lines: Brief, electric shock-like pain in a specific facial nerve distribution, triggered by light touch to specific areas, with a completely normal examination between episodes — a combination highly characteristic of this particular condition

treatment: Patricia was started on a specific medication, with the dose gradually increased to find the level that controlled her symptoms while minimizing side effects. Over the following weeks, the frequency and severity of her pain episodes reduced substantially, allowing her to eat and brush her teeth again without the same dread of triggering an attack.
discharge: She continued on her medication with regular follow-up to monitor its effectiveness and any side effects, with the option of a specific surgical procedure discussed for the future if medication alone stopped controlling her symptoms adequately.
